# Build status

The one file that says where the build is. Every run reads it first and updates it after every step. How a run works: [RUNBOOK.md](RUNBOOK.md).

## Now

- **State:** `building`
- **Stage:** 1, foundations — [plan](STAGE-1.md). Stage 2 — [plan](STAGE-2.md) — fills spare lanes.
- **Branch:** `build/stage-1`
- **Gate:** `npm run verify` and the browser checks, run by GitHub's machines on every pushed branch since 2026-11-13 (runbook, section 3). Read the result with `node scripts/github-check.mjs`. On this computer, lanes and the main folder run only `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck` and the test files of what changed.
- **Next step:** every step in the stage 1 plan is ticked; the stage is NOT called complete: it waits for the founder's check (`docs/build/STAGE-1-REPORT.md`). Its review added steps 2.92 to 2.100 (production-blocking: 2.92 to 2.95, 2.97). Land the open lanes below, then fill lanes from `node scripts/build-dashboard.mjs`.
- **Lanes:** up to 6 at once (runbook, section 3). The founder confirmed on 2026-11-12 that many builders at once is what they want. Lower the number if this computer struggles with that many.
- **Moving main forward:** allowed, only through `node scripts/promote-to-main.mjs`, which the lead runs after every landing and at the end of a run. The founder left `main` to the lead (2026-11-12) and asked on 2026-11-13 to see the commits in GitHub's statistics, which count `main` only. Since 2026-11-13 the live tracker is built from one fixed commit named in `.github/workflows/demo-pages.yml`, so the script moves `main` whenever the move is a plain fast-forward, GitHub's checks have passed on that exact commit, and no workflow that reaches the live tracker differs from `main`'s; games do not hold it back any more. Changing what the tracker is published from is a release: only the lead, in a session the founder started, with `--release-tracker`, and never from 24 hours before a game to 4 hours after. Never push to `main` any other way, and never by hand in a run.
- **Pushing to GitHub:** allowed, for the build branch (`git push origin build/stage-1`) and, since 2026-11-13, for lane branches so that GitHub checks them (the lead pushes them, builders never do; a lane branch is deleted from GitHub when its lane has landed). The founder said yes to pushing on 2026-11-12 and confirmed that the repository being public is fine. Never push or merge to `main` by hand: it is the branch the live Al-Hadi tracker site at `mrsaiyed.github.io/league-platform/` is published from, and that site is in use for real games.

States: `building` (keep the lanes full) · `waiting-for-founder` (no step in any plan can be opened until the list below is answered). The end of a stage does not stop the build (runbook, section 9).

## Needs the founder

Nothing here stops the build. Since 2026-11-13 the lead answers open product questions itself and lists them for your yes (CLAUDE.md, "Who decides what"). What is left here is what only you can do.

- [ ] Stage 1 checklist (full text with reasons in `docs/build/STAGE-1-REPORT.md`, "Your checklist"): turn on two-step sign-in for GitHub, the recovery email and Supabase, then for each new account (T-83); set up the shared password vault with emergency access (T-166); create Render, Cloudflare, Resend and a domain (and Sentry and an uptime checker), checking each price first (T-167); for the test copy put its two API keys in `.env.staging`, download Supabase's certificate and change its database password; Google sign-in key when wanted; decide on leaked-password protection (T-85) and on continuous backup's cost (T-153); in GitHub's settings turn on dependency and committed-password alerts and protect `main` from force-push and deletion. - 2026-11-14 — Fixed the flaky GitHub failure "with no test names" (cca1387; also e65f9fc, 37f6dd1 and several lanes). The log, read signed in, named it: `game-corrections.test.ts` > "not with an older correction" failed because a correction from an earlier transaction counted. The S-7 check (0009) found "this transaction's correction" by `at = now()`, and two transactions can start in the same instant (PGlite's clock ticks in milliseconds; fast on GitHub's machines). Real flaw, not only a test one: migration 0011 records each correction's transaction (`game_corrections.written_in`, `pg_current_xact_id()`) and the check asks for that. New test dates an older correction the same instant on purpose and is refused (fails on the old check). Also seen here: vitest's 'Timeout calling onTaskUpdate' under load, which vitest.reporter.ts already forgives when every file passes.
